claim: The United States has not built a new oil refinery in fifty years.
read: The line is true only if it means a large fuels refinery with full downstream capacity. EIA's January 1, 2026 count is 130 operable refineries. The newest is Texas International Terminals in Galveston, 45,000 barrels a day, first operated in February 2022. Smaller plants also came online in 2021, 2019, 2017, and 2015. The newest refinery with significant downstream capacity is Marathon Garyville, Louisiana, online in 1977 and now 617,000 barrels a day. Existing plants have added capacity since, including ExxonMobil Beaumont in 2023. No new large refinery is not the same as no new refinery.

sources.title: EIA — When was the last refinery built in the United States?

script: Late Check. One line keeps getting repeated. The United States has not built a new oil refinery in fifty years. That is true only if the sentence means a large fuels refinery. The Energy Information Administration counts 130 operable refineries as of January 1, 2026. The newest is in Galveston. It started in February 2022, at 45,000 barrels a day. Smaller plants opened in 2021, 2019, 2017, and 2015. The newest with significant downstream capacity is Marathon in Garyville, Louisiana, online in 1977. Verdict: missing context. The interesting fact is that no large new refinery has been built. The missing fact is that new refineries have.

claim: Electric cars now outsell gasoline cars in the United States.
read: That sentence is true only if battery-electric vehicles are the majority of new U.S. sales. They are not. Share has climbed, and a single electric model can top a monthly chart, but gasoline vehicles are still most of what dealers move and nearly all of what is on the road. A rising share is not a change of guard. The claim drops the denominator.

sources.title: Alternative Fuels Data Center — light-duty vehicle data
U.S. Energy Information Administration — energy explained

script: Evening Check. One line is doing a lot of work tonight. Northline Report said electric cars now outsell gasoline cars in the United States. Listen to the scale of that. Not a model. Not a month on a single chart. The claim says the electric fleet has passed gasoline. It has not. Electric share of new sales is up, and some months an electric model is the one people talk about. Gasoline vehicles are still the majority of new sales, and they are almost the entire fleet already on the road. You can be early to a transition and still misstate the present. Verdict: missing context. The interesting fact is the rise. The missing fact is the size of what it has not yet passed.

claim: The Mississippi River drains about forty percent of the contiguous United States.
read: This one matches the record. The U.S. Geological Survey describes the Mississippi River watershed as about 1.2 million square miles, roughly forty percent of the contiguous United States. A broadcast can round a figure and still be faithful when the primary source rounds it the same way. Nothing left out of the sentence changes what it means.

script: Midday Check. Not every line on the air is a trap. Bayline Desk said the Mississippi River drains about forty percent of the contiguous United States. The Geological Survey puts that watershed at roughly 1.2 million square miles, which is the same forty percent, said with a round number the source itself uses. Verdict: matches record. Round is allowed when the record is round. We will say so when it holds.

claim: The United States has not built a new nuclear reactor in fifty years.
read: The absolute does not survive the record. Watts Bar Unit 2 in Tennessee began commercial operation in 2016. Vogtle Units 3 and 4 in Georgia followed in 2023 and 2024. The fleet is old. New construction has been rare and expensive. Rarity is not absence.
script: Morning Check. An old line is back, and it is still too clean to be true. Civic Ledger said the United States has not built a new nuclear reactor in fifty years. Watts Bar Unit 2 came online in 2016. Vogtle Unit 3 entered commercial operation in 2023, and Unit 4 in 2024. That is a thin decade of construction. It is not an empty fifty years. Verdict: contradicted.
correction: An earlier draft of this check dated both Vogtle units to 2023. Unit 3 entered commercial operation in July 2023. Unit 4 entered commercial operation in April 2024.

claim: A classified briefing this week confirmed the regional blackout was caused by a foreign cyberattack.
read: Nothing on the public record confirms that sentence. A classified briefing cannot be audited from the outside, and no on-the-record finding, technical report, or utility filing has established a foreign cyberattack as the cause. Silence in the public record is not proof the claim is false. It is proof we cannot check it. Until a citable record exists, the verdict stays unverifiable.
script: Late Check. This is the one we will not pretend to settle. Night Signal said a classified briefing this week confirmed that the regional blackout was a foreign cyberattack. We cannot sit in that briefing. We also cannot find an on-the-record official finding, a technical report, or a utility filing that says what the sentence says. That does not make the claim false. It makes it unchecked. Anonymous certainty and a closed door are not sources. Verdict: unverifiable. If a public record appears, this page changes in the open.
